identity.description: Gradient-boosted ensemble of symmetric (oblivious) trees with ordered target statistics + optional ordered boosting (CPU default is Plain) and ordered target statistics — its distinguishing mechanism: raw categorical features are encoded internally without target leakage, so it is the strongest default on categorical-heavy tabular data.

emits.note: classification; Logloss training yields comparatively well-calibrated probabilities, though calibration still helps under heavy imbalance
native per-row via get_feature_importance(type='ShapValues') — exact SHAP on oblivious trees; global importances also native

learning_rate.note: when unset the library auto-derives it from iterations and dataset size (~0.03 typical)

bagging_temperature.note: INERT under CatBoost's real CPU default bootstrap_type='MVS'; only active under Bayesian bootstrap.

one_hot_max_size.note: CPU default; categories at or below this cardinality use one-hot instead of ordered target statistics

invariances.why: numeric splits are threshold comparisons on quantized borders; rescaling a feature moves border values but not the induced row partition
border quantization is built from the feature's value ORDER, so monotone transforms preserve bin membership and yield identical trees
nan_mode (default Min) maps missing numerics to a value below all observed ones so every split can separate them, and missing categoricals form their own category — no imputation required

THE distinguishing mechanism: ordered target statistics computed over random permutations encode raw categories using only preceding rows' targets, eliminating target leakage/prediction shift by construction
a non-parametric ensemble makes no assumption about the marginal or error distribution
ordered boosting was designed to counter prediction shift on modest n, so it degrades more gracefully on small data than peers; training is slower than LightGBM/XGBoost at very large n
tree predictions are piecewise-constant; outside the training range the prediction is clamped to the nearest leaf

featureStats.why: the fraction of columns that are high-cardinality categoricals is exactly where ordered target statistics beat one-hot/label encodings — the primary route-to-CatBoost signal
boosting still needs enough rows per feature for stable gradient estimates, though ordered boosting lowers the floor relative to siblings
severe imbalance makes accuracy meaningless, shifts the honest metric to PR-AUC/lift, and suggests auto_class_weights/scale_pos_weight
high missingness is where the built-in Min/Max NaN handling and missing-as-category behavior are an advantage worth citing over impute-then-linear

modelMetrics.why: if a linear model ties the GBT, the added variance/opacity of boosting is not earning its keep — a commit-linear signal
one feature owning most importance is the leakage-dominance signature the promotion gate blocks — doubly relevant here since target-statistic encodings can amplify a leaky categorical

edgeCases.condition: string/object categorical column not declared in cat_features
edgeCases.behavior: fit raises CatBoostError (cannot interpret strings as numeric)
library rejects it — categorical features must be int or string
ordered target statistics computed from very few preceding rows become noisy encodings
default Logloss underweights the minority class

driver.wrapperNeeds: cat_features column list must be forwarded to fit() from the feature-assembly dtype manifest; otherwise sklearn-compatible fit/predict/predict_proba

placementClaims.why: built-in Min/Max NaN mapping and missing-as-category handling make upstream imputation unnecessary and sometimes harmful (destroys the missingness signal)
monotone-transform-invariant: log/rank/box-cox cannot change border quantization or split structure
scale-insensitive by mechanism; standardization is wasted compute
pre-encoding destroys the ordered-target-statistics mechanism that is CatBoost's whole advantage — the docs explicitly say to pass raw categorical values via cat_features, never pre-encoded ones
